name: Stinson 10 / HW75 Voyager
summary: Pre-war three-seat high-wing tourer that became the Voyager and the forerunner of the postwar Stinson 108. About 1,000 were built before the war.

wings: High wing braced by a strut to the lower fuselage on each side
engines: Single small flat-four (65-90 hp) in a smooth, rounded cowl
fuselage: Enclosed three-seat cabin with generous glazing
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel

tellTales: Prewar three-seat high-wing with a strut each side and a tailwheel
Smooth, round cowl over a small engine
Large cabin glazing for a 1940-era light plane

confusedWith.howToTell: The 108 is the larger postwar four-seater with a bigger, deeper cowl and flat-six; this is the smaller three-seat prewar airframe.
The Cub Cruiser has a Cub-style squared-off nose and straight lines; this one has a rounder, glassier cabin and a curved tail.
The Chief is a two-seat side-by-side with a deeper, rounder fuselage and small cabin; this has three seats and bigger windows.
The Luscombe is a smaller two-seater with a different, sleeker cowl and V-struts; this three-seater is wider and has a single strut per side.
